answer: Latency Inlet Gating. Each identity registers through a hardware inlet that timestamps a challenge and forces a fixed propagation delay through a silicon delay line; the summit of valid registration requires the response to arrive inside a narrow window the operator cannot compress. A walnut-sized secure element holds the delay-line calibration, so one operator cloning software still hits the same physical floor. Spinning up N identities costs N delay-line units and N serialized registration slots, capping throughput at hardware count rather than compute.
